Definition: an eatable (includ. provender, flesh and fruit)
BiblicalUsage: The word names food, what is eaten, and it runs from the garden to the exile. God made every tree pleasant to the sight and good for food, and the woman saw the tree was good for food and took of its fruit. The queen of Sheba saw the meat of Solomon's table and there was no more spirit in her, and Daniel asked that his food not defile him with the king's meat.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe food is the first gift and the first temptation, because the same tree that fed us became the tree we stole from. I hold that God still provides our daily bread, and the table is holy when we receive it from His hand and refuse what would defile us.
